question: Can softmax full-rank attention be estimated with provable accuracy in linear time and space without sparsity or low-rank priors?
hypothesis: Positive orthogonal random features give an unbiased, low-variance softmax-kernel estimate so a linear-attention Transformer can match a regular Transformer.
contributions: FAVOR+ mechanism: positive orthogonal random features for softmax and Gaussian kernels
Theory: unbiasedness, MSE comparison with trigonometric features, orthogonality gap, uniform convergence with m=Theta(d log d)
Experiments on pixels, text and proteins

method.summary: Replace the attention block of a Transformer with FAVOR+: map queries and keys through random feature maps (positive, orthogonal) and compute Q'((K')^T V) right-to-left; causal case via prefix sums. Everything else is unchanged; implemented in Jax.
method.task: efficient attention; language modelling of proteins, text (LM1B, PG-19) and ImageNet64 pixels

datasets.name: TrEMBL (Jan 2019)
datasets.split: IID split plus held-out Pfam families as OOD; single sequences clipped to L=1024
datasets.source: UniProt TrEMBL, 139,394,261 sequences of which 106,030,080 unique
datasets.preprocessing: Concatenated variant: sequences joined with end-of-sequence token, grouped into non-overlapping L=8192 (train 4,532,224, valid 4,096)

datasets.name: PG-19
datasets.preprocessing: unigram SentencePiece, 32768 tokens; perplexity rescaled by token ratio 1.5634/1.5487/1.5359

models.name: Standard model for speed and ImageNet64/concat

results.table: Table 2, rows BID Test Performer (generalized) vs Transformer, column Accuracy

results.table: Table 2, row BID Test Performer (softmax), column Accuracy

results.claim: On unidirectional protein modelling the generalized Performer slightly beats the Transformer on test accuracy.
results.table: Table 2, row UNI Test Performer (generalized), column Accuracy

results.claim: Out-of-distribution, the Performer is slightly worse than the Transformer (UNI).

results.table: Table 2, row UNI OOD Performer (generalized), column Accuracy

results.claim: On concatenated-protein L=8192, a Transformer is memory-limited to a small variant plateauing near 19%, while the full-size Performer reaches about 24%.
results.setup: TrEMBL concatenated to L=8192; Transformer shrunk to (8,{1,2,3},256,256); Performer standard (8,6,2048,512), batch 8 per chip
results.quote: the Performer is able to train continuously to ≈24%
results.note: values read in text as approximate

results.claim: Maximum sequence length on a 16GB V100 for the regular-size Transformer in the speed benchmark.
ImageNet64 (U, L=12288) bits per dimension after 100K steps are nearly identical for ReLU, softmax and SMREG Performers.
results.setup: ImageNet64, Performer-ReLU 3.67, Performer-Softmax 3.69, Performer-Softmax SMREG 3.67, 100K steps

results.claim: Transferring pretrained Transformer weights into a Performer gives only a small non-zero starting accuracy, then recovers quickly with fine-tuning.
results.setup: LM1B, Fig 5 left, trigonometric softmax Performer from pretrained Transformer weights

results.claim: FAVOR+ attention costs O(Lrd) time and O(Lr+Ld+rd) space versus O(L^2 d) and O(L^2+Ld) for regular attention.
results.setup: r random features, bidirectional; analysis not measurement

results.claim: Positive random features have MSE going to 0 as softmax-kernel value goes to 0, whereas trigonometric features have MSE going to infinity; orthogonal features lower MSE further (Thm 2).
results.setup: theory (Lemma 2, Thm 2); empirical check Fig 4 with L=4096, d=16, 15 samples

results.claim: Trigonometric softmax features give unstable training and NaNs on PG-19; positive features with redrawing are needed to match the Transformer.
Linear Transformer (elu+1 feature map) trained with the Performer setup hit exploding gradients in all 3 unidirectional seeds and in the bidirectional run near 125K steps.
results.setup: ProGen 36-layer TrEMBL setting, same hyperparameters as Performer-ReLU

results.claim: Performer obtains the largest Long Range Arena score among scalable (>100 examples/sec) methods.
results.setup: LRA benchmark, results copied from the LRA paper (Fig 19)

limits: Accuracy gains of the generalized ReLU kernel over softmax are shown on protein data only; the text benchmarks (PG-19) show only curves in the main text.
Performer needs fine-tuning to reuse pretrained Transformer weights because of error propagation (Fig 14).
Single runs with no variance reported for most results; step counts and warmup not stated.
OOD protein accuracy is slightly below the Transformer.
Authors concede the OOD split does not guarantee a minimum distance from training sequences.
Speed benchmark is on V100/Jax; no comparison with fused exact-attention kernels (later work, not in paper).
